topic: What If Your Text Took Two Days to Get a Reply? (Vertical Short)
title: WHAT IF YOUR TEXT
TOOK A DAY?

script.beat: 0 cold open hook (0-4s): phone REPLY IN 2 DAYS
script.text: You hit send. The reply comes back in two days.
Not because they're ignoring you. Because your friend is one light-day away, and on the eighteenth of November Voyager one gets there.
Text the Moon and radio waves moving at about one hundred eighty-six thousand miles per second arrive in one point three seconds.
Text Mars and the delay stretches up to twenty-two minutes: you can make a whole sandwich before the typing dots appear.
Out at Neptune, a message takes four hours and ten minutes one way.
And at one light-day, about sixteen billion miles out, a command takes twenty-four hours each way, where Voyager one carries the Golden Record with greetings in fifty-five languages.
Who would you text first? Full film on the channel.

science.claim: One light-day is about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion km); light travels at about 186,000 miles per second; Voyager 1 reaches one light-day on 18 November 2026 at 5:16 a.m. EST after 49 years, 2 months and 11 days.
science.working: Light travels at ~186,000 miles/s; over 24 hours (86,400 s) that is ~16 billion miles (~26 billion km). From launch on 5 September 1977 to 18 November 2026 is 49 years, 2 months, and 11 days.

science.claim: The Moon is 384,400 km away with a 1.3-second one-way light delay, while Artemis II astronauts needed about three days to fly there.
science.working: 384,400 km / ~300,000 km/s = ~1.28 s (1.3 seconds one way), compared to ~3 days for crewed Artemis II lunar transit.

science.claim: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth; Mars one-way light delay ranges from 3 to 22 minutes; Neptune one-way delay is 4 hours 10 minutes and Voyager 2 took 12 years to reach Neptune.
science.working: 1 AU light time is ~8 min 20 s. Earth-Mars distance varies with orbital position, giving 3 to 22 minutes one-way light time. Neptune is ~30 AU (~4 hours 10 minutes one-way light time; Voyager 2 launched 1977, arrived 1989 = 12 years).

science.claim: Mars solar conjunction happens about every 26 months when Earth and Mars are on opposite sides of the Sun, causing communication blackouts that can last weeks.
science.working: Earth-Mars synodic period is ~26 months; solar corona blocks and corrupts radio signals passing near the Sun for weeks.

science.claim: At one light-day, a radio command takes 24 hours to reach Voyager 1 and 24 hours for the reply (48 hours round-trip). NASA celebrates Voyager's light-day on 17 November; Mars and Jupiter sit close together before sunrise on 15-16 November; the Leonid meteors peak on 17-18 November.
science.working: 1 light-day = 24 hours one-way propagation delay, 48 hours two-way. Skywatching dates from NASA's November 2026 guide.

science.claim: Voyager 1 launched on 5 September 1977 and carries the Golden Record with greetings in 55 languages, including 'Hello from the children of planet Earth.'
science.working: Voyager 1 launch date 5 Sep 1977; Golden Record audio greetings recorded in 55 languages plus music and sounds of Earth.
science.source: NASA Voyager 1 https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/ and NASA Night Sky Notes https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/skywatching/night-sky-network/novembers-night-sky-notes-light-day-away/

science.claim: Voyager 1 is heading toward star AC +79 3888 (17+ light-years away) and will pass within about 1.7 light-years of it in 40,000 years. Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away (a reply takes about 8.5 years). Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away. Voyager 2 reaches one light-day in November 2035.
science.working: Round-trip light time to Proxima Centauri: 2 x 4.24 light-years = 8.48 years (about 8.5 years).
